scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Tecktonik originated in 2002 with the 'Tecktonik Killer' parties at the Metropolis nightclub in Rungis, Paris suburbs, organized by Cyril Blanc and Alexandre Barouzdin to promote hardstyle and jumpstyle music.
The name is a pun on tectonic plates.
The founders created a visual identity with neon colors, fingerless gloves, and tight clothing.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Tecktonik was originally danced at themed club nights such as 'Tecktonik Killer' parties promoting hardstyle and jumpstyle music.
It spread through street gatherings and viral online videos, becoming a youth cultural phenomenon in France and internationally around 2007.
The dance was associated with a distinctive fashion and club culture.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Cyril Blanc and Alexandre Barouzdin are the key figures behind Tecktonik, organizing the original parties, creating the brand, and registering the trademarks.
Cyril Blanc was artistic director of the Metropolis nightclub.
Tecktonik originated in Paris suburbs but spread internationally, including to Brazil where groups like Power Rangers and Deadly Crew formed.
Tecktonik is a street dance style derived from a fusion of industrial dance, Moroccan chaabi, disco, vogue, waacking, hip-hop, and freehand glowsticking.

visual_brief.setting_notes: Tecktonik was originally danced at themed club nights such as 'Tecktonik Killer' parties promoting hardstyle and jumpstyle music. It spread through street gatherings and viral online videos, becoming a youth cultural phenomenon in France and internationally around 2007. The dance was associated with a distinctive fashion and club culture. It also appeared in music videos and at events like the Paris Techno Parade. The dance's meaning is linked to energetic self-expression and community among youth, with a commercial brand identity controlled by its founders.
